searches.note: Twenty three searches of twenty eight, five unspent. Five were restricted to a house's own domain (grosset.com.au twice, jimbarry.com, sevenhill.com.au and mounthorrocks.com once each) and are read as primary through their summaries; others blocked the house or the author's main source so the second source would be independent. One Wendouree search returned only Lake Wendouree's own history and is counted. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label words, every beat of the story, cards and questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was in one source only, or none, it was cut or said with less.
Writers' own sites met among the results (Wine with Seth, Campbell Mattinson, Chris Shanahan, Wine Anorak, The Wandering Palate) are cited neither in the fragment nor here as a second source.

tested: Founding 1981 and the Auburn building: the house's Our story page (an old milk depot) against Wikipedia (a butter and ice factory); the house wins.
The 1981 Rieslings from Watervale and Polish Hill: Wikipedia and CellarTracker. Sound.
The Polish Hill vineyard planted 1996 by the house: its vineyard page and two secondary accounts; Gourmet Traveller Wine gives 2000 as the first vintage with its fruit. Added as 1996.
Fourteen producers and the screwcap of 2000: the Clare Valley Wine and Grape Association, Australian Wine Review and others; one Scotsman piece says thirteen. Sound.
The Polish settlers: the ship August at Port Adelaide on 17 August 1856, the largest group at Hill River, by the Clare Museum, the Polish Council and the South Australian history hub. Sound.
The making: free run juice, hand picked and unfined by the house's sheets; stainless steel and no malolactic by two secondary accounts. Batches by clone and neutral yeast cut.

swaps.why: The author proposed no swap. The author weighed Sevenhill's Brother John May Reserve Shiraz against St Ignatius in report; refused as a swap: St Ignatius is the house's long running blend named for the order's founder, the pick of the plan, and no source of this check calls the reserve Shiraz the house's flagship.

rules: No living person named, no price, no score (the Decanter trophy cut), nothing volatile, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash: read across all five records after the edits. The notes on oldest and first stand on the house's claims, hedged.
codexTension: The library record p-grosset's traps and p-jim-barry's trap call Watervale and Polish Hill Clare subregions; the region has no legally registered subregions, so the fragment says localities (the author's report, confirmed). Reported, not edited.

The region record calls Clare Australia's Riesling capital and the screwcap switch by the Riesling makers together for 2000; the second stands on fourteen producers, the first is a ranking. Reported, not edited.
The library holdings line of p-grosset names the founder, a living person. Reported, not edited.
